'''Annick Gabrielle Pouquet''' (born 24 December 1946)<ref>{{Cite web|last=Congress|first=The Library of|title=LC Linked Data Service: Authorities and Vocabularies (Library of Congress)|url=https://id.loc.gov/authorities/names/n88231758.html|access-date=2020-11-30|website=id.loc.gov}}</ref> is a computational plasma [[physicist]] specializing in plasma [[turbulence]]. She was awarded the 2020 [[Hannes Alfvén Prize]] for "''fundamental contributions to quantifying energy transfer in magneto-fluid turbulence''".<ref name=":1">{{Cite web|last=Dendy|first=Richard|date=13 Jan 2020|title=The EPS Alfvén Prize 2020 is awarded to Dr Annick Pouquet|url=https://www.eps.org/blogpost/751263/337793/The-EPS-Alfven-Prize-2020-is-awarded-to-Dr-Annick-Pouquet|website=European Physical Society}}</ref> She currently holds positions in the [[Laboratory for Atmospheric and Space Physics]] and [[National Center for Atmospheric Research]] at the [[University of Colorado Boulder]].<ref name=":0">{{Cite web|title=Physics - Annick Pouquet|url=https://physics.aps.org/authors/annick_pouquet|access-date=2020-11-30|website=American Physical Society - Physics Magazine}}</ref>

The Politano–Pouquet relation, an exact [[scaling law]] for [[Magnetohydrodynamics|magnetohydrodynamic]] turbulence, was partly named after her.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Politano|first1=H.|last2=Pouquet|first2=A.|date=1998|title=von K\'arm\'an--Howarth equation for magnetohydrodynamics and its consequences on third-order longitudinal structure and correlation functions|url=https://link.aps.org/doi/10.1103/PhysRevE.57.R21|journal=Physical Review E|volume=57|issue=1|pages=R21–R24|doi=10.1103/PhysRevE.57.R21|bibcode=1998PhRvE..57...21P |url-access=subscription}}</ref><ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Politano|first1=Hélène|last2=Pouquet|first2=Annick|date=1998|title=Dynamical length scales for turbulent magnetized flows|url=https://agupubs.onlinelibrary.wiley.com/doi/abs/10.1029/97GL03642|journal=Geophysical Research Letters|language=en|volume=25|issue=3|pages=273–276|doi=10.1029/97GL03642|bibcode=1998GeoRL..25..273P |s2cid=121565391 |issn=1944-8007|url-access=subscription}}</ref>

== Early life and career ==
Pouquet graduated with a [[thèse d'état]] in [[astrophysics]] (French equivalent of [[Doctor of Philosophy|Ph.D.]]) from the [[Nice Observatory|Observatoire de Nice]] in 1976, where she studied turbulence in the presence of a magnetic field using models and direct numerical simulation.<ref name=":0" /><ref>{{Cite web|title=Laboratoire de Mécanique des Fluides et d'Acoustique - UMR 5509 - Annick Pouquet Visiting LMFA|url=http://lmfa.ec-lyon.fr/spip.php?article915&lang=fr|access-date=2020-11-30|website=lmfa.ec-lyon.fr|language=fr}}</ref> She then remained at the observatory upon graduation, eventually becoming the director of the observatory's Cassini Laboratory in 1998.<ref name=":2">{{Cite web|title=Curriculum Vitae - Annick Pouquet|url=https://sites.google.com/site/pouquetannick/CV|access-date=2020-11-30|website=sites.google.com}}</ref>

In 2000, Pouquet joined the [[National Center for Atmospheric Research]] (NCAR) at the [[University of Colorado Boulder]] as director of the Geophysical Turbulence Program and section head of the Turbulence Numerics Team, where she led efforts to investigate wave-turbulence interactions in the [[Earth's atmosphere]] and in space.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Annick Pouquet {{!}} staff.ucar.edu|url=https://staff.ucar.edu/users/pouquet|access-date=2020-11-30|website=staff.ucar.edu}}</ref> Pouquet also founded the Earth and Sun System Laboratory as the first acting director in 2004 and became its deputy director between 2006 and 2009.

Pouquet retired in 2013 and became an [[emeritus]] Senior Scientist at NCAR.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Emeritus/emerita staff {{!}} National Center for Atmospheric Research|url=https://ncar.ucar.edu/who-we-are/staff/emeritus-staff|access-date=2020-11-30|website=ncar.ucar.edu}}</ref> She also became an adjunct professor at the Department of Applied Mathematics, and a visiting scientist of the [[Laboratory for Atmospheric and Space Physics]] at the [[University of Colorado Boulder]].<ref name=":1" /><ref name=":2" /><ref>{{Cite web|date=2018-09-24|title=Annick Pouquet|url=https://www.colorado.edu/amath/annick-pouquet|access-date=2020-11-30|website=Applied Mathematics|language=en}}</ref>

== Honours and awards==
Pouquet was inducted as a fellow of the [[American Physical Society]] in 2004.<ref>{{Cite web|title=APS Fellow Archive|url=https://www.aps.org/programs/honors/fellowships/archive-all.cfm?initial=&year=2004&unit_id=&institution=National+Center+for+Atmospheric+Research|access-date=2020-11-30|website=www.aps.org|language=en}}</ref> She was awarded the [[Hannes Alfvén Prize]] in 2020.<ref name=":1" />
She became a Fellow of the American Geophysical Union (AGU) in 2023 for {\it ``outstanding contributions to understanding geophysical turbulence"}. She was recipient of the Lewis Fry Richardson Medal of the European Geophysical Union (EGU) in 2024  for her {\it ``contributions to theoretical and computational turbulence in neutral and conducting fluids, with a focus on magnetohydrodynamic turbulence and dynamo theory"} {\sl (see https://www.egu.eu/awards-medals/lewis-fry-richardson/2024/annick-pouquet/)}. She was nominated Chevalier de l'Ordre National du M\'erite (Paris/Los Angeles) in 2024 (Journal officiel de la R\'epublique Fran\c caise, texte 3 sur 88, 8 Juin 2024).
